title: Quota parameter inversion on private deployments triggering sustained 429s for affected tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A config migration that ran for private/VPC customers inverted the meaning of two rate-limiting fields (burst_duration and refill_interval) for a subset of tenants. As a result, several Dedicated/Private tenants experienced prolonged hard throttling (HTTP 429) for multiple hours because token buckets were refilled orders of magnitude slower than intended. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate remediation, and follow-up to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-10T02:11Z - On-call pager: first customer reports of persistent 429s for private tenant 'acme-data' while hosted customers were unaffected.
2026-03-10T02:25Z - Support escalated to Platform SRE and Runtime team. Initial hypothesis: quota enforcement misconfiguration rather than capacity shortage.

2026-03-10T03:00Z - Discovered config-migration job (migration-2026-03-09-ratefields) ran during maintenance window and wrote converted values to private control plane. Suspected unit/field mapping bug.

2026-03-10T04:15Z - Applied emergency rollback of migration to restore pre-migration config for 6 high-traffic tenants. Immediate reduction in 429s observed for 2 tenants; others required further state reconciliation.
2026-03-10T07:40Z - Deployed hotfix to config parser (PR #1298) to correct inversion logic and added defensive validation. Deployed to control plane and new migrations prevented.
2026-03-10T10:00Z - Reconciled token-bucket state for all affected tenants using replay and a corrective refill script; most tenants recovered by 10:30Z.
2026-03-11T09:00Z - Full verification pass and customer confirmation for 100% of impacted tenants. Incident declared mitigated. Postmortem work scheduled.
2026-03-14T14:00Z - This ticket closed after required follow-ups scheduled and changes merged to mainline.
Note: All timestamps are UTC and came from control-plane audit logs.
reproduction_steps: 1) In a private control plane sandbox, seed a tenant config with burst_duration=10 and refill_interval=60 (seconds) expected semantics.
2) Run the migration that converts these fields (migration-2026-03-09-ratefields) which erroneously maps burst_duration->refill_interval and refill_interval->burst_duration without unit conversion.
3) Observe that the resulting token bucket has refill_interval set to 10 seconds worth of minutes (unit inversion), causing refill to occur every 600 seconds.
4) Send sustained requests at previous expected throughput and observe token depletion and systematic 429s beyond reasonable burst windows.
5) Check control-plane audit entry showing migration write with mismatched field names.
mitigation_actions: Rollback: Reverted migration state to snapshot (snapshot id: controlplane-2026-03-09-2300) for affected tenants within 20 minutes of detection.
Hotfix PR #1298: Fixed config-parser so field mapping preserves original semantics and added explicit unit annotations.
State reconciliation script: ran 'bucket-reconcile-v2' to recompute token counts and refill timers for 38 tenants that retained inverted values post-rollback.
Customer comms: Sent targeted incident updates to customers listed in 'impacted_customers' and opened support cases; SOC and accounts teams notified for high-severity customers.
Monitoring: Created temporary dashboards and an alert rule for 'private.quota.inversion' to surface similar diffs in future migrations.
root_cause: A migration tool introduced during private-control-plane schema work had an incorrect mapping between 'burst_duration' and 'refill_interval' and failed to convert units consistently (seconds vs minutes). The conversion code relied on field order rather than explicit names; for private deployments a previous schema drift had swapped the canonical field ordering, which the migration did not account for. The control-plane lacked a validation gate that verifies that effective refill rates remain within expected bounds after migration.
fix_summary: Code: Migration tool updated to use explicit field names and unit metadata rather than positional mapping (merged PR #1298).
Validation: Added post-migration sanity checks that compare pre/post effective RPS and burst capacity and fail migration on >10x deviation.
Automation: Added an idempotent reconcile job that can repair token-bucket state when refills are inconsistent with config.
Docs: Updated private deployment migration runbook with pre-migration dry-run and mandatory customer-impact review for any rate/quota changes.
rollout_plan: Merge fix to main and create canary release for control plane (done).
Run migration dry-run on staging control plane and validate sanity checks (done).
Schedule safe migration window for remaining clusters where migration didn't run (planned Q2).
Enable automatic pre-migration validation and alerting to block any migration that changes effective refill rate by >2x for production tenants (done).
verification: Observed metrics: 429 rate for affected tenants returned to baseline within 40 minutes of rollback and reconciliation.
Synthetic tests: Added E2E synthetic that exercises token buckets under private config permutations; all green after fix.
Customer confirmation: 100% of impacted customers acknowledged service restoration; two customers requested compensation conversations via Customer Success.
Longer-term: 7-day baseline check configured to ensure no regressions in quota behavior across Private clusters.
postmortem_followups: PM to lead a retro and coordinate customer communications follow-through (owner: Lina Cho).
Add migration unit-tests and require code owners approval for migration-tool changes (owner: Marco Hernandez).
Instrument control-plane audit logs to emit a 'rate-migration-delta' metric and create a PagerDuty rule for >5x unexpected change (owner: SRE team).
Run a one-off audit across all Private clusters to detect similar field mismatches from prior migrations (owner: Infra Ops).
